items.title: Fed rate hike 'not urgent', says John Williams; Austan Goolsbee warns against 'playing with fire'
items.summary: Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams stated there could be one more interest rate increase before year-end. He emphasized that the central bank is not in a hurry to act immediately as it awaits more economic data. Williams projected that inflation might end the year at approximately 3.5% before returning to the Fed's target by 2028.

items.title: Euro Falls to 16-Month Low as Hawkish Fed Bets Boost Dollar
items.summary: The euro fell to its weakest level in 16 months as expectations that the Federal Reserve will further boost interest rates supported the US dollar.

items.title: Fed's Williams sees no urgency for next Fed rate hike
items.summary: Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams said on ​Tuesday that the U.S. central bank has time to weigh economic data before deciding when to hike interest rates again, adding one more increase is likely ‌before the year ends.

items.title: Inflation isn't done: Interest rates likely to rise more, Fed Governor Michael Barr warns
items.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr warned that interest rates may rise further to combat inflation, which is still significantly above the 2% target. Despite strong economic performance, officials anticipate one more rate hike this year as they focus on achieving price stability.

items.title: Prospect of Fed pulling too far back on communications poses volatility risk, Musalem says
items.summary: Too big a pullback in the US central bank's communications could lead to higher and more volatile interest rates and ​inflation if the public and businesses are left to guess ‌how it would react to different economic developments, St. Louis Federal Reserve President Alberto Musalem said on Tuesday.

items.title: Equities end slightly lower as bond yields hold near multi-decade highs
items.summary: US stocks ended the session slightly lower on Tuesday, as government bond yields continued their ascent ahead of inflation and labor market ​data, while investors assessed comments from Federal Reserve officials for the path of interest rates.

items.title: Stocks drop and oil rises as Hormuz hopes fade
items.summary: HONG KONG — Asian stocks mostly fell and oil prices extended gains Tuesday as hopes for a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz fade amid expectations the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates again next month.
